description: SQE Renovate config. Local dry-run: renovate --platform=local --dry-run=full.
The local platform reads files from git, so this file must be committed to be picked up.
Canonical remote is GitLab; GitHub is a mirror. Nothing here is platform-specific.

packageRules.description: Fold routine Rust minor/patch bumps into one PR; majors stay separate for individual review.

description: Cargo treats a 0.x MINOR bump as semver-BREAKING: 0.12 -> 0.13 is an incompatible release.
Renovate classifies it as `minor`, so the rule above folded ten breaking bumps into a single
37-package 'routine' MR (!728) -- reqwest, sqlx, sha2, hmac, base64, toml, governor,
datasketches, rusqlite, opentelemetry. That MR could not regenerate Cargo.lock, said so in an
'Artifact update problem' comment, and merged anyway; main then failed to resolve at all.
Keep pre-1.0 minors out of the routine batch so each arrives reviewable on its own.

packageRules.description: DataFusion/Arrow/Parquet are API-coupled and pinned in lockstep with the vendored iceberg-rust fork. Group into one reviewed PR (overrides the rule above); a version skew here breaks the build, and a bump usually means re-checking the vendor rebase.
Container images in the quickstart/test docker-compose stacks (Polaris, MinIO/RustFS, Keycloak, etc.). Non-automerged: a bumped image can silently break a quickstart's assumptions.
AWS CDK deps live only in the quickstart demo projects; examples, not shipped code, so lower urgency.
Aikido CI platform includes (ci/templates/*.yml @ ref); keeping the guardrails/test/deploy templates current warrants a dedicated PR.

description: jsonwebtoken is held below 10 deliberately. 11 ships NO crypto provider by default,
so a tree that type-checks perfectly panics on every JWT verification at runtime --
which is exactly how it reached main unnoticed (!728, then !738 to fix, then reverted).
A bot cannot validate that, because `cargo check` and `cargo build` both pass.
Any move to 10+ needs an explicit provider feature and a test that verifies a real
token, so it has to be a human change, not a version bump.
apache/ranger is held below 2.9 because of SPARK, not because of SQE.
SQE itself is fine on 2.9.0: `make test-access-control` is 42 of 42 there,
because grants post to /service/plugins/secure/services/{grant,revoke}/{svc}
and policies and tags come from the secure download twins.
What breaks is the Kyuubi Spark plugin. It picks the secure download URL
only under Kerberos: isKerberosEnabled(ugi) is !forceNonKerberos AND
UGI.isSecurityEnabled() AND ugi.hasKerberosCredentials(), and forceNonKerberos
can only turn secure mode OFF. No property turns it on. This stack runs
KERBEROS_ENABLED=false, so the plugin calls the unauthenticated
/service/plugins/policies/download/{svc}, which 2.9.0 refuses with HTTP 400
unless ranger.admin.allow.unauthenticated.download.access is enabled. The
basic-auth credentials in ranger-spark-security.xml are sent, but the PATH
stays the unauthenticated one, so they buy nothing.
Bumping Kyuubi does NOT lift this, and that is the trap. Verified:
kyuubi-spark-authz-shaded_2.12 1.11.1 and 1.12.0 (latest) bundle
byte-identical Ranger classes, RangerAdminRESTClient sha256 684c0eda... built
2025-02-14, because Kyuubi's pom pins ranger.version 2.6.0. The version to
watch is ranger.version inside kyuubi-spark-authz's pom, not Kyuubi's own.
Measured on 2.9.0: `make test-access-control` 42 of 42, parity demo 5 passed
2 failed with 'Permission denied: user [alice] does not have [update] privilege'.
A bot cannot validate this: the container starts, the health check passes,
and `docker compose up` succeeds. Moving to 2.9+ needs a Kyuubi build whose
bundled Ranger selects the secure URL when a basic-auth filter is present,
plus a green `make test-access-control-spark`.
The Ranger quickstart's postgres is held on 13.x deliberately. A bump to 18.3
broke the whole stack: postgres 18 stores data in a major-version-specific
subdirectory, so an existing volume is unreadable and the container exits 1.
ranger-admin never starts, which takes out make test-access-control and
make test-access-control-spark.
The trap is that a FRESH volume starts fine, so CI can look green while every
developer with an existing stack is broken. A bot cannot validate a data-directory
migration, so moving majors here has to be a human change: pg_upgrade or a
documented volume reset, plus a check that Ranger 2.8's schema is happy.
